transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I'd like to discuss Mr. Lewis's potential enrollment in our remote-monitoring program following his heart-failure discharge. As we all know, before I can finalize any enrollment and configuration decisions, we need to review the clinical, technology, and home-support requirements together. I'd like to start by hearing from cardiology nursing on Mr. Lewis's clinical needs, then from clinical informatics on the technology side, and from social work on his home-support situation. Who would like to begin?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I can start with the clinical side. Mr. Lewis's most recent echocardiogram shows a left-ventricular ejection fraction of exactly 32%, and our program's clinical eligibility criterion is an ejection fraction of 35% or lower, so he meets the criterion. I have the result from the specialist's signed report.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: On the technology side, I should flag an important consideration: Mr. Lewis's apartment has no reliable internet service. However, our informatics team has a cellular monitoring hub reserved for him. The hub must be configured during device setup for the connected scale and blood-pressure monitor to transmit readings. So we can support him, but the cellular hub configuration is a required step in his setup.
